questions: Did your walking difficulty begin suddenly?
Did it begin after an injury, fall, or surgery?
Is pain the main reason you cannot bear weight?
Do you feel weakness in either leg?
Do you feel weakness in both legs?
Do you have numbness or tingling in either leg?
Do you have back pain?
Does pain travel from your back into either leg?
Have you lost control of your bladder or bowel?
Do you have numbness around your groin or buttocks?
Has your walking difficulty been progressively worsening?
Have you had episodes in which the weakness or walking difficulty comes and goes?
Do you have problems with balance or coordination even when you are not in pain?
Do you have stiffness or spasms in your legs?
Do you have weakness, numbness, or clumsiness in your arms or hands?
Did these walking problems begin during childhood?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological disease?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a spine disorder?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a muscle or nerve disease?
Do your joints frequently dislocate or partially dislocate?
Do you have unusually flexible joints?
Do you have fever, unexplained weight loss, or a history of cancer?
Are you currently able to stand or walk without the crutches?
Have you recently developed difficulty speaking, seeing, swallowing, or controlling one side of your body?

results: 1. Complete neurological examination, including cranial nerves, eye movements, tone, reflexes, plantar responses, coordination, proprioception, and sensory testing
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): genuine axial and lower-limb rigidity on passive movement
MRC power in all four limbs: 5/5 throughout
2. Observed gait examination, including tandem gait, heel-to-toe walking, turning, Romberg testing, and assessment of gait with and without crutches
Romberg test, repeated with distraction: negative
3. MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium contrast
4. MRI of the entire spinal cord with and without gadolinium contrast
MRI cervical and thoracic spine: normal cord
5. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and thyroid-stimulating hormone
full blood count, renal and liver profile: normal
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
6. Serum vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, copper, vitamin E, and folate
vitamin B12 with methylmalonic acid: normal
7. Serum HIV antigen/antibody, syphilis serology, and Lyme disease serology
8. Serum inflammatory and autoimmune testing, including ESR, CRP, ANA, and rheumatoid factor
9. Serum very-long-chain fatty acids and adrenocorticotropic hormone
10. Lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal-fluid cell count, protein, glucose, oligoclonal bands, IgG index, infectious studies, and autoimmune/paraneoplastic testing
CSF cell count and differential: normal
CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index: normal
CSF culture and viral PCR: normal
12. Genetic testing for hereditary spastic paraplegia and adult-onset hereditary ataxia panels
hereditary ataxia / repeat-expansion panel: no expansion
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Stiff-person spectrum disorder (predominantly axial and lower-limb stiff-person syndrome), most likely autoimmune anti-GAD65–associated disease

ALTERNATIVE: Seronegative stiff-person spectrum disorder, including anti-amphiphysin–associated paraneoplastic disease

ALTERNATIVE: Early atypical parkinsonian disorder with predominant axial rigidity

ALTERNATIVE: Functional neurological gait disorder with superimposed or misinterpreted axial rigidity
